Salcedo et al. 2017 Science is linked on the record; not needed, since the deposit rules the project OUT and metadata is permitted to do that.

Unblocks the project parked on 2026-10-07: the PAPER defers growth conditions to a cited reference, but the submitters state the inoculation and post-inoculation handling in the BioProject Description itself.

U. virens / rice dual RNA-seq; the deposit mixes in-planta inoculated panicles with in vitro cultures. Both arms are non-field, so the project is out of the cohort on setting without splitting the libraries.

F. graminearum libraries across three stated growth conditions: in-planta pathogenic growth on Brachypodium, saprophytic growth on dead plant substrate, and axenic starvation culture. Fungal transcriptomes, not plant foliar tissue; non-field on every arm.

Shu et al. 2017. B73 grown in field plots at the Central Crops Research Station; ears needle-inoculated in situ at 21-22 DAP and harvested from the plots on an hpi timecourse. Field-exposed throughout, so a new vocabulary value rather than 'field (excised, lab-inoculated)', which describes material brought indoors. Ears were bagged until inoculation, which limits natural inoculum reaching the kernel specifically.
A. flavus / F. verticillioides are the known pathogens, so under the two-evidence standards a finding here must be a pathogen BEYOND those two.

Every sequenced sample derives from single pustules increased to pure cultures on susceptible wheat inside a BSL-3 facility. The field metadata on this deposit (geo_loc_name 'Uganda: Kalengyere Research Station', and Ethiopia/Italy collection records) is where the ISOLATE came from, not where the sequenced plant grew. This is the field-origin/controlled-sequencing trap in its archive form.

Wheat blast strain B71 genome project. The paper's own data statement calls the deposited RNA-Seq 'cultured', i.e. axenic mycelium; the WGS and Hi-C runs are not RNA-seq at all. BioSample env_local_scale 'wheat field' is the isolate's origin.

Trzmiel et al. 2025. Field barley leaves from Polish experimental fields and crop production areas, pooled into ONE HTS library, symptomatic (stunting, leaf discoloration). Run-scoped because this BioProject is an umbrella: the other two runs are WSMV isolates (Poland 2022, Ukraine 2023) belonging to a different study and still need their own paper. Pooling means a co-infection call here cannot be attributed to a single plant.
Sampled for stunting and leaf discoloration. The study itself reports BVG in co-infection with BYDV-PAS and wheat dwarf virus, so a known-pathogen stratum.

AvrYr7 effector study (ANU). Every BioSample is sample_type 'spores', so the sequenced material is Pst urediniospores and not plant tissue at all. The env_local_scale 'Field' and the lat/lons are the ISOLATE's provenance; isolates span 1972 to 2020 and four countries, which no single sequencing experiment could have sampled directly. A new value rather than 'in vitro culture', which would be false: Pst is an obligate biotroph and cannot be cultured axenically. Leaving the value at how the spores were increased would be an inference the metadata does not support; what IS evidenced is that this is pure pathogen material.

ZmEREB92 seed-germination study. Surface-sterilised seeds on wet filter paper in a germination box at 28 C in the dark, sampled at 0 and 6 h of imbibition. The material is imbibing seed, not foliar tissue, so the project is out of scope twice over.

Blumeria graminis f. sp. triticale compared across wheat and triticale hosts. The GEO growth protocol gives the chamber outright (20 C, 12 h light / 12 h dark) and the treatment protocol gives the inoculation, with samples at 48 dpi.

C. graminicola staged through pre-penetration appressoria, biotrophic and necrotrophic phases during infection of maize leaf sheaths. A 24 / 36 / 60 h staged series cannot be obtained without inoculating, which is what makes this evidence rather than inference. GSE34632's growth protocol defers to Mosquera et al. 2009 Plant Cell and so is not usable on its own; the staging is.
The wild-type-versus-mutant companion to PRJNA151285, sharing GSE34632 and adding GSE71919. Comparing isolates through the same staged in-planta phases requires artificial inoculation.

68 classified runs, the largest single item in the STAT cereal tail. The deposit belongs to the Plant Cell 2023 transcriptional-landscape paper, NOT to the two papers that surface first on an accession search: the PNAS Rgs1 paper states outright that it analysed 'publicly available RNA-seq dataset', and 10.3390/ijms26104618 is a receptor-gene meta-analysis. Guy11 spray- or leaf-drop-inoculated onto 21-day-old CO39 and Moukoto seedlings over an 8-point time course from the moment of inoculation.
Wheat stripe rust. The methods say artificial inoculation at the two-leaf stage, which also rules out field material: a two-leaf-stage inoculation time course is a seedling assay.
Pst-infected versus mock (CK) wheat leaves at 7 dpi, and the sequenced input is named as those samples, so the link is to the sequenced material rather than to a companion experiment.

Two papers cite this 2-run accession and it is not resolved which generated it, but both describe artificial inoculation of the sequenced material (F. graminearum point-inoculated spikelets at 12 and 48 hpi in one, Pst-inoculated two-leaf-stage seedlings in the other). The verdict therefore does not depend on which owns the deposit, which is why it can be written without resolving that question.

Australian Pgt pathotypes behind the Science 2017 AvrSr50 paper. collection_time runs 0H / 15H / 10DPI, and a post-inoculation time series cannot be obtained without inoculating; the hosts are cv. Morocco and cv. Sonora, universally susceptible lines used to increase rust. The collection_date values (1925, 1954, 1969) are the isolates' provenance, not the sequencing experiment, which is the same archive-form trap as PRJNA1267768.

Western Canadian stripe rust survey. These 18 samples had RNA extracted DIRECTLY from single-lesion infected leaf tissue taken from commercial crop fields, with no purification step, so the sequenced material is naturally infected field plant tissue. Keyed on the isolate NAME, not on collection_method: the attribute reads 'Infected leaf harvested' for 33 of the 35 RNA-seq samples because it records how the ISOLATE was obtained, not what was sequenced, and keying on it put 33 runs in the field arm against the paper's stated eighteen. The bare province codes (AB/BC/SK plus three digits) are exactly those eighteen; every purified isolate carries a descriptive name instead (BC_SPI-n, 13_Rust_n, a cultivar name).
Sampled as single lesions, so selected for disease. host_disease is 'Stripe rust', which puts these runs in the known-pathogen stratum: a finding has to be a pathogen BEYOND Pst.

The other 17 RNA-seq samples, purified to single-pustule isolates through at least one round of inoculation and spore recovery, with RNA taken from urediniospores. Pure pathogen material, not plant tissue; same value as PRJNA1457771. Listed explicitly rather than as a negation of the field arm, because the grammar has no negation and because an unreliable attribute is exactly where a silent catch-all would hide a misassignment. override=yes is required and is not cosmetic: the first version of this rule keyed on collection_method and wrote 'field' to 33 runs, and narrowing the rule does NOT retract what the old one wrote - a rule at the same precedence tier cannot replace an existing _rule value without it, so 15 runs would have kept a value no surviving rule produces. The handful of WGA runs whose isolate names match also take this value; they are DNA and out of scope either way, so scoping the rule to RNA-Seq would only have stranded them at the stale value instead.

One cultivar (Drifter) infected with a panel of different Z. tritici strains is a designed strain comparison, and a strain panel cannot be assembled on one cultivar without inoculating it. Two papers cite the accession (10.1099/mgen.0.001136 on lncRNA pangenomes, 10.1002/pld3.484 on Triticeae lineage-specific genes); neither is in the text cache, and neither is needed, because the deposit's own description rules the project OUT and metadata is permitted to do that.

The four samples the paper names as silica gel-preserved survey samples from south-west Australia, collected 2012 and 2013. Naturally infected field wheat, and all four carry 'species in sample: High Plains wheat mosaic emaravirus, Wheat streak mosaic virus' on their BioSample, so the co-infection is already documented in the archive. Exactly the kind of sample this chapter is about.
Virus survey samples, collected because they were infected. Two viruses are already known to be present, so a finding has to be a pathogen beyond WSMV and HPWMoV.

The one sample in the deposit that is not a survey sample: it came from an infected leaf of a maintained culture host, sweet corn cv. Snow Gold. A culture host is a plant kept infected to propagate the virus, so the material is not field-collected even though the virus originally was.

Pt76 reference-genome project. These libraries are dormant and germinated urediniospores, so pure pathogen material. The November 2018 collection from the CSIRO Canberra field site produced the ISOLATE, which was then purified through single-pustule isolation and pathotyped; nothing field-collected was sequenced. The rule also catches the Hi-C and Illumina DNA libraries, whose names likewise say 'from spores'; that is the correct value for them, so they are left matched rather than excluded by a LibraryStrategy clause.

The in-planta arm, at 6 and 9 days post inoculation. A dpi series on a purified, pathotyped isolate is an inoculation experiment. Keyed on LibraryName, which names the material outright ('RNAseq library of Pt infected wheat leaves 6 days post infection rep1'). The Nanopore and WGA runs match neither rule and are left without a setting.

Sekhon et al. 2019 maize senescence. The paper separates two plantings and only one is the sequenced material: the diversity panel was phenotyped across Wisconsin 2011, Wisconsin 2013 and Pendleton 2017, while B73 and PHG35 for the TRANSCRIPTOMIC experiment were grown in six-row field plots at Clemson University Simpson Research Farm in Pendleton in summer 2017. Every BioSample carries geo_loc_name 'USA: South Carolina, Clemson University Farm Pendleton', which agrees. Tissues are leaf, ligule, sheath and internode, all aerial.

A senescence time course with no disease or chemical treatment anywhere in the text: fungicide, pesticide, insecticide, inoculation, infection, lesion and greenhouse all score zero on a full-text scan. This is the stratum where a single unreported pathogen is itself the finding.

Stated as summer 2017; the BioSamples give no date at all. Year only, because the paper gives no finer resolution than the season and the dev_stage values (15 / 30 / 33 / 36 days after anthesis) are a developmental axis, not calendar dates.

Unblocks the project held out this morning on the no-manuscript rule. The paper states what the submitters stated: field-grown KN5585 and zmlecrk1-c2 infected with R. solani and sampled at 72 hpi. Same shape as PRJNA418364, field-exposed throughout with a pathogen added in place.
R. solani is the known pathogen, so a finding here must be a pathogen BEYOND it. Mock-treated plants are in the deposit as the comparison arm.

Maize inbred J1259 grown in the field at 60,000 plants per hectare with surrounding guard rows, then inoculated in place 15 days after artificial pollination by injecting F. verticillioides through the husk with a syringe. Field-grown and field-inoculated, so the same value as PRJNA418364 and PRJNA1161467.

F. verticillioides is the known pathogen. Note for the analysis stage: the paper also reports that measures were taken to prevent insect infestation, so this field was not chemical-free even though no fungicide is named.

Naturally senescing B73 ear leaves at 0, 14 and 21 days after silking, from plants cultivated at the experimental station of Fudan University. The paper's own Methods 4.1 describes a growth room and a greenhouse, but that covers the Arabidopsis, the B73 seedlings and the transgenic lines - NOT the sequenced ear leaves, which are mature open-pollinated plants three weeks past silking and could not be greenhouse seedlings. This is the field-phenotype / controlled-sequencing trap running in reverse: the paper's stated growth conditions belong to the companion experiments and the archive holds the ones for the sequenced material. The no-manuscript bar is met by the paper; the setting value rests on the submitters' own growth_protocol.

Wheat cv. Su11 inoculated with the virulent Pst CYR31 and the avirulent CYR23 to produce paired compatible and incompatible interactions, sampled on an hpi series. A designed pathotype contrast cannot be obtained without inoculating.

Rice cv. Shennong 9816 at 28 +/- 2 C under 16 h light / 8 h dark, inoculated at the three-leaf-one-heart stage with a laboratory-preserved R. solani AG1-IA strain activated on PDA. The chamber is named, so the value can be more specific than 'lab inoculation'.

Rice sampled uninfected and R. solani-infected at 12, 24 and 48 hpi, with the accession named in the same passage, so the link is to the sequenced material. The agroinfiltration of N. benthamiana elsewhere in this paper is a companion assay and was what a looser screen matched on first.

Rice cv. BPT-5204 sampled at 1, 2 and 5 days post inoculation with R. solani. A dpi series is an inoculation experiment. The source is a bioRxiv preprint, which still counts as an available manuscript.

Field pathogenomics, settled by Notes S1. RNA was extracted DIRECTLY from the leaves or stems of Pgt-infected bread wheat plants collected in the UK, Germany, France, Uganda and South Africa; there is no second extraction protocol in Notes S1 and no increase step before sequencing. Notes S1 section 3 is the controlled work and it is a different experiment: urediniospores harvested from the 20 UK 2022 samples were multiplied on susceptible cv. Vuka under 16-h light at 18/12 C for VIRULENCE PROFILING, not for RNA-seq. The Viewpoints article itself carries no methods at all, which is why this sat blocked. Notes S1 counts 52 samples against ENA's 53 runs (27 UK not 26, 12 South Africa not 11, and no Uganda row), most likely one technical replicate plus a country mis-entry; it does not affect the verdict, because the single extraction sentence covers every sample in the deposit.
Every sample is a Pgt-infected plant, collected because it was infected. Puccinia graminis f. sp. tritici is therefore the known pathogen and a finding here has to be a pathogen BEYOND it.

The paper says 'leaves or stems' without resolving which sample is which, and Dataset S2 was not supplied. Recorded as the pair rather than guessed per run; both are aerial, so cohort membership is unaffected either way.
